newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel leader led siege by cell phone - report.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel leader led siege by cell phone - report.

text.p: Marxist guerrilla leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini used a cellular telephone to direct the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, a Peruvian newspaper said on Friday.
"It is known that Cerpa Cartolini gave orders for the takeover via (cellular) telephone, from some place in Peru whose whereabouts is not known," the daily Expreso said.
Anti-terrorism police sources could not immediately confirm this version, although they said it was very likely.
Cerpa took over the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) after the 1992 jailing of previous leader Victor Polay, who is serving a life sentence.

The 20 MRTA fighters who besieged the residency during a lavish cocktail party on Tuesday confiscated guests' cellular phones and were using them to transmit messages to local media and relatives of their nearly 400 hostages.

Peru's anti-terrorism police had been carrying out a massive manhunt for Cerpa and the current leader of the better-known Maoist Shining Path guerrilla movement, Oscar Ramirez Durand, alias "Comrade Feliciano."

Despite these operations, however, security experts had prior to the siege been constantly warning that the government was dangerously under-estimating and letting down its guard against the threat from leftist guerrillas.
